questions.prompt: What is the colleague test (Anthropic's golden rule)?

options.text: Ask a colleague to write the prompt for you
If a colleague with minimal context would be confused by your prompt, the model will be too
Only send prompts during work hours
Always copy a colleague's best prompt

questions.explanation: The model is like a brilliant new employee with no context on your situation. If a colleague couldn't follow the prompt without asking questions, the model will have to guess.

questions.prompt: Which details make a prompt more specific? Select all that apply.

options.text: Writing the whole prompt in capital letters

questions.explanation: Audience, goal, reason, length, and format/tone remove guesswork. Capital letters add emphasis, not information, and can cause over-reaction in newer models.

questions.prompt: Markers such as triple quotes or XML-style tags that separate your instructions from pasted content are called ____.
questions.explanation: Delimiters show where content begins and ends, so the model doesn't treat the content as instructions.

questions.prompt: Which version of a formatting rule follows the advice to explain the why?

options.text: This will be sent as an SMS, which can't display tables or formatting, so write plain sentences only.

questions.explanation: With the reason (SMS can't show formatting), the model can also avoid bold text, bullets, and other things you didn't list.

questions.prompt: Match each common mistake to its description.

pairs.right: Several unrelated tasks crammed into one request
"Fix this" without the error or the code

questions.explanation: Each mistake forces the model to guess: which task, which shared memory, which missing input, or which of two incompatible instructions to follow.

questions.prompt: Put the letters of S.P.E.C.IFY in order by what they stand for.
questions.explanation: S.P.E.C.IFY stands for Style, Purpose, Examples, and Constraints, a final-pass checklist from Mark Austin's book.
